findings.quote: the armies broke up and marched away from the place
findings.problem: ὧν καὶ παραγενηθέντων ἐξ αὐτῆς ἀνέζευξαν αἱ δυνάμεις: ἐξ αὐτῆς is the adverbial idiom 'immediately, at once' (sc. ὥρας), not 'from the place'; ἀνέζευξαν = broke camp.
findings.proposed_fix: the armies at once broke camp and withdrew

units.note: Minor, not in the error classes: Εὐμένης ... πεισθεὶς μετὰ μεγάλης χάριτος (Tium) is rendered 'as a generous favor', leaving out πεισθείς ('being persuaded'); left unflagged.

findings.problem: τῶν ἀφρακτιτῶν: from ἄφρακτος, an open or undecked ship, so the men of the undecked ships. Upper-deck rowers would be θρανῖται, which is not what the Greek says.
findings.proposed_fix: each of the crews of the undecked ships

units.note: ἀφρακτιτῶν is an unusual form, so the exact meaning is not certain. The reading as crews of undecked ships is the likelier one.

findings.quote: when it still did not seem likely that the Lycians would once again revolt
findings.problem: ὅσον οὔπω δοκούντων πάλιν ἐπαναστήσεσθαι τῶν Λυκίων: ὅσον οὔπω means 'all but now, on the point of', so the Lycians seemed about to rise again. The English reverses this and says a revolt seemed unlikely.
findings.proposed_fix: when the Lycians seemed on the point of rising again
